topic.title: Advanced C++ & Modern Features
topic.description: Templates, Move Semantics, Smart Pointers, Lambdas, and STL Algorithms.

questions.title: Move Constructor vs Copy Constructor
questions.explanation: d1 calls Default constructor (D). std::move casts d1 to an rvalue reference, triggering the Move constructor (M) for d2. d1 is in a valid but unspecified state. Assigning d1 to d3 calls the Copy constructor (C).

questions.title: Lambda Capture by Value
questions.explanation: The lambda captures x by value. The 'mutable' keyword allows the lambda to modify its internal copy of x (printing 15). The original x in main remains 10.

questions.title: Template Instantiation
questions.explanation: print(5) deduces int, calling the int specialization (I). print(5.5) deduces double, calling the generic template (T). print<int>(5.5) forces the int specialization, implicitly converting 5.5 to 5 (I).

questions.title: Unique Pointer Transfer
questions.explanation: std::unique_ptr cannot be copied. Moving p1 into p2 transfers ownership, leaving p1 as a null pointer (1 for true), while p2 now points to 10.

questions.title: Shared Pointer Reference Count
questions.explanation: Initially, the reference count is 1. Inside the block, sp2 shares ownership, making it 2. When the block ends, sp2 is destroyed, dropping the count back to 1.

questions.title: constexpr Evaluation
questions.explanation: constexpr functions can be evaluated at compile time if arguments are constant expressions (like square(4)). If arguments are runtime variables (like square(a)), they execute at runtime.

questions.title: std::remove on Vectors
questions.explanation: std::remove shifts non-removed elements to the front (1, 3, 4). It does NOT change the vector's size. The elements past the new logical end are left in a valid but unspecified state (often leaving old values behind).

questions.title: Perfect Forwarding
questions.explanation: wrapper uses a forwarding reference (T&&). std::forward preserves the value category. 'a' is an lvalue, so it calls process(int&). '10' is an rvalue, so it calls process(int&&).

questions.title: Exception Re-throwing
questions.explanation: The naked 'throw;' inside a catch block re-throws the current exception, passing it up the call stack to be caught by the outer block.

questions.title: decltype keyword
questions.explanation: decltype(y) inspects the declared type of y, which is int&. Therefore, z is also an int reference to x. Changing z to 20 changes x.

questions.title: CRTP (Curiously Recurring Template Pattern)
questions.explanation: CRTP achieves static polymorphism. The base class casts its 'this' pointer to the Derived type at compile time, resolving and calling Derived::implementation without virtual table overhead.

questions.title: Variadic Templates
questions.explanation: The variadic template recursively unpacks arguments, printing the first and passing the rest, until the base case (empty print()) is reached.

questions.title: std::initializer_list
questions.explanation: Uniform initialization with braces maps perfectly to std::initializer_list constructors, printing the number of elements passed.

questions.title: Type Traits (is_same)
questions.explanation: int and const int are different types (0). std::decay strips const/volatile qualifiers and references, making 'const int&' decay into 'int' (1).

questions.title: std::any
questions.explanation: std::any can hold any type. It was reassigned from int to std::string. Attempting to extract it as an int throws std::bad_any_cast.

questions.title: std::variant and std::visit
questions.explanation: std::variant holds one of the specified types (currently float). std::visit applies the generic lambda to the currently active type.

questions.title: Return Value Optimization (RVO)
questions.explanation: Due to mandatory Copy Elision (RVO) in C++17 and later, the object is constructed directly in the memory location of 'o'. No copy or move constructor is called.

questions.title: std::bind
questions.explanation: std::bind wraps the function and maps the second argument (5) to 'a' and the first argument (10) to 'b'. It calculates 5 - 10 = -5.

questions.title: Fold Expressions
questions.explanation: C++17 fold expressions expand (... + args) into (1 + (2 + (3 + 4))), returning the sum 10.

questions.title: Structured Binding
questions.explanation: C++17 structured bindings allow unpacking tuples directly into named variables.
